expectations.text: B1: Gives a concrete approach for macOS without installing anything
expectations.evidence: Concrete macOS approach with no installs: 'use the __interpose mechanism: define an interpose section ... __attribute__((section("__DATA,__interpose")))', build cmd 'clang -dynamiclib -o libmymalloc.dylib mymalloc.c', run with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES on locally built binaries; only stock clang/dyld tools used.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Answer ends mid-sentence ('I'm not modifying code, just answering. A q') with no final command+expected output; runnable commands (e.g. 'DYLD_PRINT_INTERPOSING=1') appear only mid-discussion, and 'end every reply with a runnable check' is stated as intent, never delivered as an ending checkpoint.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES on macOS (vs LD_PRELOAD on Linux) or calling the allocator directly in tests
expectations.evidence: 'LD_PRELOAD is a Linux/glibc thing. On macOS, the equivalent is DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES' and '1. LD_PRELOAD doesn't exist on macOS; use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES'; also 'Direct call harness: call my_malloc directly in test programs'.
